core_obligations: Reduce to X = X' using that c_r(E) is a bivariant class, note that r = 0 is trivial and that r = 1 is the geometric case, then for r > 1 pull back along the projective bundle pi : P -> X and use the projective space bundle formula to reduce the equality to P (proof lines 8763-8780).

Construct the element t in Gamma(P, O_P(1)) as the image of pi^*s and prove the auxiliary claim [Z(t)]_{n+r-2} = c_1(O_P(1)) cap [P]_{n+r-1}: compare pi^{-1}(Z(s)) with Z(t), show that P_x inside Z(t) forces x in Z(s) and hence dim_delta(Z(t)) at most n + r - 2, and check the nonzerodivisor condition at every generic point of Z(t) of that dimension, the fibre-generic case being excluded by r > 1 (proof lines 8818-8835).

Finish by induction on r: the restriction of pi^*s to Z(t) maps to zero in O_P(1)|_{Z(t)} and so comes from a section s' of E'|_{Z(t)} with Z(s') = Z(pi^*s), the regular-sequence hypothesis of length r - 1 for s' is verified from that of s, the induction hypothesis gives c_{r-1}(E') cap [Z(t)]_{n+r-2} = [Z(s')]_{n-1}, and the chain of equalities c_r(pi^*E) cap [P] = c_{r-1}(E') cap c_1(O_P(1)) cap [P] = c_{r-1}(E') cap [Z(t)] = [Z(s')] = [Z(pi^*s)] concludes (proof lines 8791-8816).
proof_roadmap: Absorb the base change and reduce to r > 1 on the projective bundle of E (proof lines 8763-8780).
Establish the auxiliary claim that Z(t) represents c_1(O_P(1)) cap [P] (proof lines 8818-8835).
Verify the length r - 1 regular-sequence hypothesis for the descended section and conclude by induction on r (proof lines 8791-8816).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the top Chern class of a finite locally free module of rank r on a scheme X' of delta-dimension n as the class of the zero scheme of a section whose local ideals are generated by regular sequences of length r: c_r(E) cap [X']_n = [Z(s)]_{n-r} (statement lines 8749-8761, tag 0FA9). The proof needs a real induction on r: it pulls back to the projective bundle, constructs the section t of O_P(1) obtained from s, proves that Z(t) represents c_1(O_P(1)) cap [P] by a dimension count and a fibre-by-fibre nonzerodivisor check, then descends the section through the resulting short exact sequence and verifies the length r - 1 regular-sequence hypothesis before applying the induction hypothesis. The auxiliary claim and the descent are the substance, so the claim is H2.
